description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit. Sacrifice with 4.f3! and attack the black king.

drills.briefExplanation: 4.f3! exf3 5.Nxf3 Bg4 6.h3 — sacrifice, develop, and question the pin.
drills.description: White to play. Black took on e4 — sacrifice with the Blackmar-Diemer 4.f3!.
drills.explanation: The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: White sacrifices a pawn (and sometimes two) for a ferocious initiative. After 4.f3! exf3 5.Nxf3 White has open e- and f-files, fast development, and direct attacking chances — the classic BDG compensation. Club players fear it for good reason: one slow move by Black and the attack crashes through.
drills.name: The f3 Sacrifice

drills.briefExplanation: 5.fxe4 Nxe4 6.Qf3! Nc6 7.Bb5 — trade, hit the knight, and pin in return.
drills.description: White to play. Black declined with 4...Bf5 — trade and attack the knight.
drills.explanation: Against the solid 4...Bf5 decline, White keeps the pressure by trading: 5.fxe4 Nxe4 6.Qf3! — the queen hits the knight and eyes f7. After 6...Nc6 7.Bb5 White pins in return, keeping the initiative. The gambit may be declined, but the pressure isn't.
drills.name: Trading Into Attack
